rationale:
ROUND 2 of migration 516 (round 1 = REVISE, gated by prior_art_librarian). Three objections were right and are built; the gating one was a stale document, now fixed at source rather than argued around.

(A) GATING, prior_art_librarian: 'the schema's own landmine ledger carries an entry keyed exactly to this operation: any migration writing a marker-suffixed key into {workflow,steps,<step>,config}'. The entry is real and the footprint matches - but its finding EXPIRED on 2026-08-20 when ecc419bd1 shipped, and two corrections beneath it already said so, including one naming migration 515 as the first live adopter. The seat matched the heading, which still read 'parses on input_mapping but NOT YET in a step's action config'. That entry's own closing paragraph had ALREADY predicted this failure in as many words - 'a reader, human or council seat, matches on the heading and the footprint, not on the third paragraph' - and recorded that it had happened once before, to a different migration. So the fault is the document's, not the seat's, and arguing my case would leave the trap armed for the next author. FIXED AT SOURCE: the heading now names both binary versions (INERT up to v1.0.1320, LIVE from v1.0.1321) and states the surviving trap in a form with no shelf life - 'a marker the reading binary does not parse applies cleanly, reports success and changes nothing' - which stays true on either side of any roll, in either direction, since a rollback makes it live again. The prescription applied is the entry's own.

(B) editquality, medium - RIGHT and it was the real defect: the migration hard-coded two (agent, step, action) tuples taken from a TOP-LEVEL jsonb_each census, which is exactly the descent that cannot see a wire nested in a sub_workflow or substeps body. The SAME landmine as (A)'s sibling entry (footprint validation.WalkSteps) prescribes the remedy verbatim: 'if a migration must touch every carrier, drive it from the recursive walk rather than a hand-typed list - a list is a snapshot of whatever your census could see.' REBUILT: apply, VERIFY and ROLLBACK are now driven by one recursive walk containing NO path literals, descending every object to any depth. It converts every step config carrying an unmarked related_pages wherever it lives; ABORTS if a discovered carrier runs an action other than the two whose absence-handling was read (discovery widens what we SEE, it must not widen what we silently accept); and refuses to succeed on zero carriers found, because '0 rows updated, COMMIT' is the shape that reads as a clean apply. VERIFY now asserts the GLOBAL postcondition - no unmarked carrier survives anywhere, every marked one holds the intended path - instead of re-checking the two paths it just edited. Dry run against live data (COMMIT swapped for ROLLBACK): '516: converted 2 related_pages carrier(s)', then '516 OK: 2 marked related_pages? wire(s), 0 unmarked carriers left anywhere', then ROLLBACK.

(C) editquality, medium (the acks edit bundles migration 515's plan_sections.page_type entry, unrelated to 330): accepted as a fair reading, kept deliberately, and here is the reason - 515 is ANOTHER session's adopter that landed while this was in review, and the gate I built exits 1 on ANY unacknowledged live wire. Omitting its entry would leave a gate that fails for a reason unrelated to whoever next runs it. The entry is sourced from 515's own migration header and its author has been told to correct it if it misstates their case. I would rather carry the coupling visibly than ship a guard that is red on arrival.

(D) guardian, medium x2: filed as 'add' rather than 'config_change' - noted, and the operation vocabulary is the gate's, not the file's; the file is a new SQL migration whose EFFECT is a config change, and its header says so in the first line. On the ledger point: a _HOLD file is deliberately outside the runner's sweep, so its apply cannot be ledger-recorded automatically - the header now says to record the apply in the lane NOTES, which is the estate's documented substitute (the runner refuses --record-only on a sidecar). That is a real residual of the _HOLD mechanism rather than of this file.

Everything else from round 1 stands: the marker is live on v1.0.1321, absence-safety was read at the consumer first-hand, and the file is still HELD behind migration 512's demand control (tool-generator runs since its boundary: still 0).

edits.rationale: Same recursive walk as the apply, for the same reason: a rollback driven by a hand-typed list would miss a nested carrier and leave it converted with no record. Verifies zero marked wires survive and the unmarked ones are restored.

Live config census 2026-08-21: exactly two steps carry a related_pages wire (tool-generator/save_tool -> create_tool_component, tool-deployer/deploy_tool -> deploy_tool_to_site), both to input_data.spec.related_pages.

Conflict instrument 2026-08-21: tool-generator/related_pages 27 rows, last 2026-08-20 09:50:10Z; tool-deployer ZERO rows all-time - so the second step's inclusion is prophylactic and the migration says so.
Migration 512's verification test, quoted from the lane handoff: 'Pass = reason 0 while related_pages STILL FIRING (if both go quiet the instrument died and the zero means nothing)'.

Measured 2026-08-21 ~11:4xZ: SELECT count(*) FROM orchestration_states WHERE owner_agent_type='tool-generator' AND created_at > '2026-08-20 17:38:34Z' returns 0 - eighteen hours, no demand, so neither 512 nor 516 can be verified today and the ordering is real rather than theoretical.

Dry run against live data 2026-08-21 (same file, COMMIT replaced by ROLLBACK): both snapshots taken, both updates applied, VERIFY printed '516 OK: both tool build steps declare related_pages? = input_data.spec.related_pages', then ROLLBACK - nothing written.
plan.risks: Applying this before 512 is verified would silence both tool-generator classes at once and make 512 permanently unverifiable - which is why the file is _HOLD with that as its stated condition, and the whole reason it is not simply applied today. The second step (tool-deployer) has no logged rows, so its conversion is prophylactic: if some caller of deploy_tool_to_site were relying on the searched value, this removes it silently - I judge that unlikely to the point of being the desired outcome (the searched value is another tool's pages by construction), but it is the one behaviour change here with no instrument behind it. After apply, 330's verification needs fresh tool-generator demand (~16 runs/24h historically, but 0 in the last 18 h) and its instrument-alive control must come from another agent's class. This does not close 330's general half - an unmarked wired-but-empty field anywhere else still falls through - which stays candidate 2, gated on the 269-pair unsampled remainder. ROUND 2 addition: the discovery walk now decides WHICH configs get edited, so its abort-on-unknown-action guard is what bounds it - a carrier running an unread action stops the migration rather than being converted. That is deliberately stricter than the hand-typed version it replaces, which would simply have ignored such a carrier.
